newsitem.title: FRANCE: French GAN plans 591 job cuts - paper.
newsitem.headline: French GAN plans 591 job cuts - paper.

text.p: French state-owned insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) was due to announce plans to cut staffing levels by 591 at a meeting with a staff works committee on Wednesday, daily Les Echos said.

A GAN spokeswoman contacted by Reuters said there would be a day-long meeting of the works committee on a "jobs adjustment plan" but declined to provide further details and trade unions at the group were not immediately available.

Les Echos said new GAN chairman Didier Pfeiffer planned to speed up staff reduction after taking over from Jean-Jacques Bonnaud, who had been planning to trim employee numbers by 500 over two years before he was fired by the government.
The newspaper quoted CFDT union member Jacques Dubaele as saying "We challenge the very validity of plan without economic justification".
Le Monde newspaper said in an edition to appear on Wednesday afternoon that unions had called on staff to stop work briefly on Wednesday morning.
The government has temporarily suspended the privatisation of GAN's banking unit CIC, a sale that was supposed to raise funds to prepare GAN itself for privatisation.
European Commissioner Karel Van Miert said recently he was expecting the government to announce new state aid for GAN, which newspapers suggest could be in the region of 10 billion francs.
The company itself has declined to comment on possible further state aid, which would add to another one approved by Van Miert last year, and the finance ministry has yet to reveal its plans.
